text: The sergeant's sent me a pupil? He must think highly of you. Or very poorly of me.
Here. Notes of an Old Angler: Hesk's late husband wrote it, next door. Read it and you'll fish as he did, for the rest of your days.
Open your bag ({key_bag}) and click the book. Or rest and take Read from the wheel ({key_wheel}). Then up the long stair to Master Isao, with my blessing.
Ah. A reader? No. You have the look of someone who reads only what's carved on a cannon.
Brother Aldous. I keep the chapel's books and the island's records, and I answer questions. Slowly.

menu.text: Ask. I have all afternoon, and the books have all century.

choices.text: How do I read a book?
What are charts and lore books?
How do I get into things here?
I'll let you get back to it.

text: A manual teaches you for good. Quicker legs, a surer arm, a steadier hand on the rod. Read once, keep forever.
What you've read goes on your shelf. Your ship's cabin will have one: a captain's library, and proof you can spell.
Click a book in your bag and read it. Or sit down for a rest and take Read from the action wheel ({key_wheel}): it reads the first book you haven't.
Books come from chests, merchants and old libraries. A book you've read is used up. The knowledge stays.
Charts mark what lies on the sea ahead of you: wrecks, merchants, worse. Read one and look at your map.
Lore comes in sets. Read a whole set and the sea gives something back. Don't ask me how. I only file them.
Sergeant Vey opens the skill map once he's seen you fight. Master Isao, up the long stair, reads your Edy.
Tackett sells refits once his sloop is yours. And Haldor won't forge for a wanted captain, so keep your name off the posters.
The bell rings for the boats that come home and once more for the ones that don't. The cross in the close is for them.
The names go in my records. It's the only voyage everyone finishes.

bye.text: Go gently. And return anything you borrow, especially books.
